findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled and can skip
findings.body: update() loads the pre-image with getById(), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() is false when the IdP is linked to a missing or disabled organization (or when the organization provider is disabled), even if the stored enabled flag is true. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate treats that wrapper as "not a login IdP". If the update also makes the raw model ineligible (enabled=false, hideOnLogin, link-only, or broker-public cleared), both predicate checks fail and the method returns without invalidating the getForLogin list keys. Those lists were built from the JPA enabled/hide/link/public filters, so they still contain the IdP. After the org is enabled again, getForLogin keeps returning it, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only re-checks isEnabled(), not hideOnLogin/linkOnly/broker-public, so a hidden or link-only broker can show up on the login page until some other event drops the cache. Compare against the delegate/raw model (or always invalidate login keys on update).

findings.title: getForLogin cache drops provider order
findings.body: Delegate getForLogin results are collected with Collectors.toSet() and then copied into a HashSet before the stream is returned. That discards the stable order previously produced by getAllStream (typically alias or creation order). Login pages sort with a comparator that is usually guiOrder, and the default guiOrder is the same for every broker, so the stable sort keeps HashSet iteration order. Brokers therefore shuffle between requests. Preserve encounter order (for example LinkedHashSet) when caching ids and when building the result stream.

findings.title: Login-cache test cleanup targets alias "alias"
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates idp-alias-0..20 but registers cleanup as testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (also at the idp-alias-20 create). That resource is not one of the created providers, so the 21 brokers are left in the shared test realm. Later tests that count or list identity providers can fail or see extra login IdPs, and the new assertions never check that the cached ids are the expected aliases rather than only a size.
